questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How plastic was invented
Why supermarkets are closing
Why whales and other sea animals are dying in the oceans
Our dependence on plastic and how to use less
questions.why: They talk about our 'addiction to plastic' and what could be done to solve the plastic crisis.

questions.q: Why is plastic such a problem, according to Rob?
options: It is very expensive to make
It doesn't break down quickly, so it stays around
It is too heavy and too difficult to recycle properly
It is made from natural materials
questions.why: Rob says it doesn't decay very quickly, so it 'hangs around for a very long time'.

questions.q: How much of the plastic produced each year is single-use?
options: About 40%
About 4%
About 60%
Almost all of it
questions.why: Rob says 400 million tonnes is produced each year and 40% of that is single-use.

questions.q: According to Lucy Siegle, what conflict do people feel about plastic?
options: They want to recycle but don't know how
They like plastic but it is too expensive
They're horrified by it but told they can't live without it
They want to buy less plastic, but the shops simply won't let them
questions.why: She says we're horrified by what we see, yet told we can't live without it, creating 'psychological dissonance'.

questions.q: What change does Lucy Siegle say she is now seeing?
options: People are buying more plastic
Awareness is turning into people taking action
Governments are banning plastic
People have stopped caring about the problem
questions.why: She says 'awareness has peaked and it's going over into activism'.

options: Going completely plastic-free straight away, from the start
Recycling everything you use
Only buying food from markets
Reducing the flow of plastic into your life
questions.why: She says stopping the flow of plastics is easier and more effective than going plastic-free from the outset.

questions.q: Why does Lucy Siegle mention the UK's supermarket culture?
options: Because most people's plastic comes from supermarket shopping
Because supermarkets have already stopped using plastic
Because she works for a supermarket
Because supermarkets are cheaper than small shops
questions.why: She says many tips for decreasing the flow of plastic are about 'getting round supermarket culture'.

questions.q: What does Rob think about the future of plastic?
options: It will disappear within a few years
It will soon be replaced by glass and other natural materials
It is useful, so it will take a long time to go
It is not really a problem
questions.why: Rob says plastic is useful for many things, so it will be a long time before it disappears.
